real_qa.q: What was Joaquin Garay's role in Walt Disney's The Three Caballeros?
real_qa.r: Joaquin Garay played Panchito, the parrot who sang all the songs in the movie. The Three Caballeros was the third film Walt Disney made, and Val Garay met Walt Disney as a kid and has an original cel from the film.

real_qa.q: How did Val Garay's grandfather escape working in the Mexican gold mines?
real_qa.r: Val Garay's grandfather was working seven stories down in a gold mine in El Mineral Del Oro, Mexico when a man fell from the top and splattered in front of him. After witnessing this, he decided he was out of the mining business and became a mechanic or engineer instead.

real_qa.q: When did Val Garay leave Stanford School of Medicine to pursue music?
real_qa.r: Val Garay was in his first year of graduate school at Stanford School of Medicine planning to be a vascular surgeon when he left to move to Los Angeles with his friend Ron Dudley in 1967. His parents had a strong negative reaction, but years later when he won Grammys for Betty Davis Eyes, his father said he would forgive him.

real_qa.q: What was the Bobby Gray Trio's significance in Val Garay's musical education?
real_qa.r: Val Garay's uncle, his father's brother, was an incredible guitar player who led a trio called the Bobby Gray Trio that played in the Bay Area for 60 years. His uncle could sing any song in any key and follow on guitar, and he taught Val how to play guitar.

real_qa.q: What was the Autumn Records label and its connection to early San Francisco rock bands?
real_qa.r: Autumn Records was a record label owned by Tom Donahue that signed bands including the Beau Brummels. Tom Donahue also ran a club called Mothers in North Beach where live performances took place, and he managed the San Francisco Mime Troupe before starting the label.

guest.bio_context: Val Garay is a Grammy Award-winning producer and engineer who started as a musician and guitarist in bands throughout the San Francisco Bay Area in the 1960s. His father, Joaquin Garay, was a famous singer and actor who appeared in over 50 films including Walt Disney's The Three Caballeros. Garay attended Stanford University on a scholarship with a major in medicine and was accepted to Stanford School of Medicine, where he planned to become a vascular surgeon before leaving to pursue music in Los Angeles.
